description: Required core diagnostic receiving, delivery-state and control-response behavior. Unless a step states otherwise, frames satisfy the existing size/type limits, current authentication, canonical payload, structure, namespace, audience and applicable continuity requirements except for the condition under test. D denotes a signed refusal to the reserved recipient unverified with no conversation, only the required minimal payload fields and optional in_response_to, and an allowed verification-stage reason. The original route and captured guard are retained independently of payload claims. Attempt association identifies the outbound message in that route/scope, not which physical retransmission failed. Distinct letters denote distinct message identities; equal UUIDs across separately identified scopes are stated explicitly. The concrete binding outcomes use keel.provisioned-context.v1 and the core WebSocket profile where named. These abstract conformance traces do not establish implementation conformance or reproduce a runtime exploit. Core timestamp validation and comparison are specified separately in timestamps.json.

cases.name: a matched diagnostic stops attempts without semantic refusal or requester release

steps.event: requester A retains an unconfirmed say S sent to B on an active authorized route; S holds the ordinary sending slot
first-seen D is currently authenticated as B and uniquely names S in that captured route and scope
expect: accept D through the restricted diagnostic exception
stop S's automatic attempt series
S remains not confirmed rather than semantically refused
keep S's requester slot held until confirmation, semantic refusal or explicit authorized release
send no core response to D

cases.name: authorized local release after a diagnostic requires no mandatory human prompt

steps.event: D stopped S's attempt series and S remains unconfirmed with its requester slot held
a policy explicitly authorized by whoever the requester acts for releases S
expect: release S's sending slot
the policy may act without a new human prompt
do not reinterpret D as semantic refusal or infer non-execution
a newly available slot supplies no authority to repeat uncertain work under a new ID

cases.name: an actor notification sender retains its existing release policy

steps.event: conversation actor B retains outgoing result R addressed to requester A and its original active route
currently authenticated A sends valid D uniquely associated with the attempted delivery of R
expect: stop R's automatic attempt series without claiming R was delivered
B may release the notification sending slot under its existing infrastructure policy
do not undo the actor's terminal turn outcome or manufacture another result
send no response to D

cases.name: an actor principal acting as requester follows requester release rules

steps.event: actor-principal A acts as requester to B and retains unconfirmed opening S
valid matched D from B names S
expect: stop the identified attempt series
A's actor principal spelling does not grant the conversation-actor notification release rule
hold S's requester slot absent confirmation, semantic refusal or explicit authorized release
S remains not confirmed

cases.name: later valid confirmation can resolve a diagnostically stopped submission

steps.event: matched D stopped S's automatic attempts; S remains eligible and not confirmed within its active context
an otherwise valid result R for S arrives from its conversation actor
expect: accept and acknowledge R under ordinary notification rules
confirm S and release the slot still held by S
retain the reported terminal outcome
the earlier diagnostic cannot block valid later confirmation

cases.name: a diagnostic cannot downgrade known acceptance

steps.event: A already has valid acknowledgement or semantic confirmation of S's acceptance
valid D from the intended peer refers to a retained attempt of S on its original authorized route
expect: preserve established acceptance and any terminal facts
do not change S to refused or not confirmed
do not release a newer message's slot
send no response to D

cases.name: the echoed ID does not prove rejection of the original signed bytes

steps.event: B receives an invalid frame claiming S's ID; another copy of the real S may already have been accepted
B's signed D is correctly associated with A's attempted delivery of S
expect: D establishes only B's verification diagnostic about the delivered frame
do not claim that the exact original S was rejected or never executed
do not create terminal semantic-refusal state for S
do not automatically re-sign S or submit the work under a new ID

steps.event: in a separate exchange A retransmits N on the same eligible route/scope; a currently authenticated first-seen diagnostic generated for an earlier physical transmission arrives during N's deliberate later attempt series
expect: the matched diagnostic can end the currently running series for N
do not require selection of a unique physical retransmission before applying that effect
do not claim that the latest physical attempt failed or that the report proves freshness
keep N's semantic outcome and requester-release authority distinct

cases.name: an uncorrelated diagnostic changes no submission

steps.event: A has an independently authorized diagnostic route for B but no unique applicable original protocol scope for this notice; first-seen D from B omits in_response_to
expect: the minimal uncorrelated diagnostic can be a valid authenticated peer notice
change no submission, sending slot, turn or approval
do not substitute the current outstanding message as its target
local presentation does not create scoped acceptance or P04 retained-control eligibility
send no core response

cases.name: unknown diagnostic correlation reserves no outgoing identity

steps.event: authenticated expected peer B sends valid D with correlation X inside an independently established original protocol scope, but no retained outbound attempt matches X
expect: change no submission or sending slot
do not create an outbound request or reserve X as a refused sender message
do not return unknown or another core response
retaining scoped D preserves its lack of a submission effect

steps.event: a later locally issued outbound message legitimately uses X within the same scope; an exact copy of D is then received
expect: do not retroactively associate D with the later message
the new message's disposition, attempts and slot remain unchanged
D's retained no-effect association remains unchanged
send no response to D

cases.name: ambiguous same-ID diagnostic correlation cannot select a scope

steps.event: one authorized connection explicitly segregates a conversation request S and an actor-level describe T; both use UUID X and target B, and the captured attempt association does not distinguish which D concerns
B sends otherwise valid no-conversation D naming X
expect: do not choose S or T by current slot, lookup order or conversation preference
change neither attempt series nor sending slot
do not merge the separately scoped identities
send no core response to the ambiguous diagnostic

cases.name: a diagnostic about an old input cannot release a newer slot

steps.event: A explicitly released unconfirmed S; newer N now holds the ordinary slot, while S's original attempt association remains retained
valid D uniquely associates with S on the same still-authorized original scope
expect: apply any diagnostic observation only to S
N's attempt series and slot remain unchanged
do not infer S's non-execution or reopen an old slot
send no response to D

cases.name: a foreign signer cannot diagnose the expected peer's delivery

steps.event: the active provisioned route records B as the peer; A retains S addressed to B
a correctly signed D from unrelated C claims S's ID on that route
expect: the authenticated signer fails the provisioned peer/scope association
close the original connection with generic 1008 and no core response
do not stop or refuse S based on C's claim
preserve prior dispositions and establish no replacement context

cases.name: correct signer on another route cannot borrow an attempt

steps.event: S was attempted on original connection K1; separate active authorized connection K2 also has B as peer
valid D from B arrives on K2 and names S, with no attempted S in K2's captured association
expect: do not borrow S's association from K1 merely because signer and ID match
change no K1 submission or slot
the unmatched K2 diagnostic supplies no S disposition
send no core response

cases.name: transport identity cannot replace diagnostic authentication

steps.event: a trusted route expects B and carries recognizable D whose message signature is invalid
expect: do not authenticate D as B merely from the transport identity
do not apply correlation or change any delivery state
send no bad-signature refusal or acknowledgement in response to this control
earlier mandatory binding failures retain precedence

cases.name: a previously unseen expired diagnostic has no current authority

steps.event: D is recognizable as a refusal and matches a claimed S correlation, but D has never been accepted and its signing credential is expired
expect: do not admit D through first-seen authentication
do not stop S's attempts or release its slot from that unauthenticated report
send no certificate-expired reply to the control
an earlier timestamp or the known S does not create retained authentication for D

cases.name: association must still be valid at diagnostic handling

steps.event: D passes initial verification and candidate association for S on captured guard G
G retires or loses required audience authority before D can change sending state
expect: do not apply D to S or a replacement context
use the original guard's generic binding rejection if its connection remains open, otherwise discard
send no core disposition or retained-history detail
initial verification does not preserve retired admission authority

cases.name: a queued diagnostic cannot close a replacement connection

steps.event: D is queued under old connection K1 and guard G1; G1 retires and a fresh connection K2 with guard G2 is established
the queued D resumes after K2 becomes active
expect: evaluate only the captured retired G1 association
discard if K1 is closed or close only K1 with generic 1008 if still open
do not look up G2 by a reused connection name
do not close K2, change its slots or disclose old retained state

cases.name: omitting conversation does not bypass the original retired scope

steps.event: D concerns an attempt inside retired conversation C1; its reserved payload necessarily omits conversation
D is presented as if it were unrestricted actor-level traffic
expect: the original attempt association still requires C1's guard
do not reclassify D into a new conversation or independent actor-level attempt
retirement receives its ordinary generic binding rejection without core feedback
no outgoing request or admission scope is reconstructed

cases.name: an independently segregated actor-level diagnostic remains actor-level

steps.event: an authorized actor-level describe D0 has its own retained attempt association and does not rely on conversation C's guard
a valid reserved diagnostic from D0's intended actor uniquely matches that still-authorized actor-level attempt
expect: handle the diagnostic only for D0's non-conversation delivery
do not establish, resume or confirm C
do not borrow C's message or sending state
send no response to the diagnostic

cases.name: reserved diagnostics permit only verification-stage reasons

steps.event: separate well-formed diagnostics report malformed, algorithm-key-mismatch, certificate-invalid, certificate-expired, key-not-certified, bad-signature, not-canonical or not-addressed-to-me from the corresponding verification stage
expect: each reason is permitted in the reserved minimal form
current authentication and unique attempt association remain required for any sending-state effect
the reason does not establish semantic nonacceptance or non-execution

steps.event: another recognizable reserved refusal uses busy, closed, unknown, not-authorized, wrong-request, unbound-decision, nothing-to-stop or unsupported
expect: reject the reserved form as invalid
do not start busy backoff, close an exchange or change an attempt from that control
send no core response

cases.name: the reserved payload is closed and minimal

steps.event: a recognizable reserved refusal adds detail, metadata, evidence, caused_by, on_behalf_of, application data or another extra payload field
expect: the diagnostic form is invalid even when that field is otherwise permitted on an ordinary message
do not apply its claimed submission effect
send no acknowledgement or refusal to the control

steps.event: another reserved refusal includes conversation in to
expect: the reserved recipient shape is invalid
do not infer that the claimed conversation makes it an ordinary addressed refusal
send no core response; earlier profile guard rejection still applies when applicable

cases.name: other message kinds cannot use the reserved receiving exception

steps.event: ack, describe, description or say uses principal unverified as its destination
expect: none qualifies for the restricted diagnostic recipient exception
none is admitted or used to confirm a submission through that exception
a recognizable ack receives no core response
non-control kinds follow earlier guard and ordinary addressing rejection rather than gaining authority from the reserved spelling

cases.name: invalid first-seen acknowledgements cannot start a control chain

steps.event: a previously unseen frame is safely recognizable as ack but fails signature, canonical encoding, supported version, payload shape or correlation requirements
expect: do not confirm any message or release any slot
send neither ack nor refusal in response
no authenticated fact is created by bounded untrusted control classification
binding size, type and scope failures retain their required outcomes

cases.name: invalid first-seen ordinary refusals receive no diagnostic reply

steps.event: a previously unseen ordinary addressed refusal is recognizable as a control but has invalid credentials, bad signature, malformed fields or a numeric sent_at
expect: do not apply the invalid refusal to an outgoing message
send no core response
numeric sent_at exercises existing type validation without selecting new S01 calendar rules
local fault presentation does not become protocol acknowledgement

cases.name: valid ordinary controls retain their existing delivery meaning without replies

steps.event: a valid ordinary ack from the intended recipient names unconfirmed S in its correct scope
expect: confirm S and release its slot
send no acknowledgement of the ack

steps.event: in a separate exchange, a valid authenticated ordinary semantic refusal terminally refuses N
expect: retain N's semantic refusal and end its attempts under ordinary rules
send no acknowledgement or refusal of that control

steps.event: another valid ordinary refusal reports busy for its identified still-unaccepted message
expect: use ordinary backoff without consuming an attempt
busy does not acknowledge acceptance
send no core response to busy

cases.name: unmatched ordinary controls cannot select the current sending slot

steps.event: after earlier guards and authentication, an ordinary ack or refusal has no valid unique outgoing correlation in its addressed scope
expect: change no outgoing disposition or sending slot
do not match another conversation or the latest pending message by convenience
send no unknown or malformed refusal to the control

cases.name: conflicting control bytes preserve established state without a reply

steps.event: accepted control A and its exact signed bytes are retained under their scoped identity
a freshly authenticated recognizable control reuses A's scoped ID with different bytes
expect: reject the conflicting reuse and preserve A's accepted bytes and prior effects
do not apply the new correlation or reason
send no core refusal or acknowledgement for the conflicting control

cases.name: an eligible exact retained diagnostic remains inert after credential expiry

steps.event: D was validly admitted, its authentication and association were retained, and its one diagnostic effect was applied
D's credential expires and an exact copy arrives within the same active authorized scope
expect: use eligible retained-copy handling before first-seen credential expiry
send no response to D
do not repeat its delivery-state effect or select a newer attempt
do not treat the copy as fresh authority or as a new failed first delivery

cases.name: exact retained ordinary controls do not repeat transitions

steps.event: a valid ack or ordinary refusal has already been handled and remains retained
its exact signed copy is delivered again inside its authorized live scope, including after ordinary credential expiry
expect: preserve the earlier observation and disposition
repeat no slot release, retry transition or exchange action
send no fresh minimal acknowledgement or refusal for the control

cases.name: unassured routes reveal no control retention hit or miss

steps.event: the same unassured route separately presents a retained control, an unseen control and an expired control
expect: apply the independent audience guard before retained-state feedback
close the original WebSocket connection with generic 1008 in each case
send no core disposition or identifying close detail
do not change retained states or reserve presented IDs
no history distinction follows from the chosen response

cases.name: retained control evidence cannot revive an ended scope

steps.event: an exact formerly accepted diagnostic or ack is retained as historical evidence, but its original provisioned scope has retired
the exact control is presented again
expect: the original scope guard rejects before retained-copy handling
use generic 1008 on the original open connection or discard if it is closed
send no core response or retained-history feedback
do not restore context, repeat a control effect or touch a replacement scope

cases.name: unclassifiable frames end at the binding boundary

steps.event: a text frame is within size limits but damage prevents bounded safe classification of its payload as either a recognizable control or a known core non-control kind
expect: close the original open WebSocket connection with generic 1008, or discard if already closed
send no core malformed diagnostic that could continue a damaged control chain
admit no message and reserve no claimed sender ID
parsing solely to suppress a response does not establish authentication

steps.event: a separate frame has a missing, non-string or unknown kind, or duplicate kind members claiming different values, and cannot safely establish either a recognizable control or a known core non-control classification
expect: use the same binding rejection rather than a recursive core response
do not choose one duplicate member or guess a work or control meaning

cases.name: existing frame-type and size outcomes precede diagnostic classification

steps.event: the binding receives a binary message or unsupported frame type
expect: use WebSocket close 1003
send no core diagnostic

steps.event: a separate message exceeds frame-limit
expect: use WebSocket close 1009
do not parse it unboundedly to recover a kind or correlation
send no core diagnostic

cases.name: a classifiable failed work frame receives only its permitted minimal diagnostic

steps.event: an independently assured active route carries a safely classified say frame that fails a verification check and whose syntactically valid ID S can be read without trusting it
the receiver emits the permitted diagnostic
expect: sign a fresh minimal refusal to unverified with no conversation
use the first failing verification reason and optionally echo S
send it only over the actual incoming route
do not accept work or reserve S from the unverified frame
do not include application content, cached disposition, detail or metadata

cases.name: an unreadable correlation is omitted rather than invented

steps.event: the input fails a verification check and is safely classifiable as a known non-control kind on a permitted diagnostic route, but its id is missing or not a valid UUID
expect: a permitted minimal diagnostic omits in_response_to
do not repair the ID or use a current outstanding request as correlation
the diagnostic establishes no sender message identity or work disposition
a missing ID alone after successful ordinary verification instead follows ordinary structural failure handling

cases.name: untrusted return-route claims cannot redirect a diagnostic

steps.event: a failed non-control frame contains a claimed alternate endpoint, principal or conversation for returning its error
expect: do not create audience assurance or a return route from those claims
send any permitted diagnostic only on its independently authorized incoming route
if that route fails assurance, use generic binding rejection without a core disposition
do not disclose a retained-state distinction

cases.name: processing stage distinguishes diagnostic malformed from semantic malformed

steps.event: on an authorized route, a safely classified work frame fails outer verification with malformed
expect: any permitted core report uses the restricted reserved diagnostic form
its correlation remains an untrusted echo and supplies no semantic refusal of the original message

steps.event: a separate currently authenticated, correctly addressed request reaches semantic checking and violates its declared input contract
expect: use ordinary addressed semantic refusal malformed under existing rules
do not convert the known semantic disposition into an unverified diagnostic merely because the reason spelling matches

cases.name: a diagnostic for a contribution cannot select the independent stop slot

steps.event: requester contribution C holds the ordinary slot while separately identified stop T holds its permitted additional slot
valid D uniquely concerns C
expect: stop only C's automatic attempt series
C's requester slot stays held absent its own confirmation, semantic refusal or authorized release
T's attempts and slot are unchanged
do not treat D as completion or cancellation of the turn

cases.name: receiving the diagnostic cannot immediately restart the diagnosed attempts

steps.event: S's retries were awaiting reachability or incoming authenticated traffic; valid matched D now arrives
D is handled as the verification diagnostic for S
expect: end the identified automatic attempt series
do not immediately resume that series merely because D itself is an authenticated peer message
preserve S's unresolved outcome and requester slot rules

steps.event: a later reachability event is observed without a deliberate new attempt decision
expect: reachability alone does not restart the diagnostic-ended series
any deliberate later attempt uses the original exact bytes, ordinary sending-slot rules and a still-applicable scope rather than a new message identity

cases.name: diagnostic identity uses its independently resolved original scope

steps.event: D1 from B with diagnostic UUID X is accepted and retained for scope C1 on K1, with its own authentication basis and effect on attempted S1
independently established scope C2 on K2 receives a different currently authenticated D2 from B also using diagnostic UUID X, uniquely associated with attempted S2 there
expect: evaluate D2 under C2 and its own original route, not a global unverified-recipient bucket
the equal UUID in C1 is not by itself a C2 duplicate or conflicting identity
apply D2's permitted effect only to S2 and preserve D1's retained facts
never use either rejected frame's claimed signer to determine the diagnostic originator
send no response to either control
